validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: the Kenai Kachemak Pipeline (KKPL) is a real, documented Alaska intrastate gas transmission pipeline, confirmed independently via (1) Alaska DNR Division of Oil & Gas's own pipeline-services record (dog.dnr.alaska.gov, a state land-management/ROW-lease agency), (2) the Regulatory Commission of Alaska's 2014 Docket P-14-025 consolidation notice, which names 'Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, LLC (KKPL)' explicitly as one of the four applicant entities, (3) Harvest Midstream's own corporate history page, and (4) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects register, which independently carries a 'Ninilchik Pipeline' project attributed to operator 'Kenai Kachemak Pipeline LLC' (EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Aug 2026 release (EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx), sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 293: Completed 2003-10-01, AK, Miles 33, Cost ($ millions) 25, 12-inch diameter, intrastate/State authority) -- four distinct origins (two AK state agencies, the current private operator, and a federal statistical agency), none tracing to GEM or to each other. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an operating (Status), gas (Fuel), transmission (PipelineType) intrastate pipeline -- DNR's page explicitly and repeatedly calls it a 'natural-gas transmission pipeline.' DUPLICATE: this row's segment ('Kenai Kachemak Pipeline') is geographically and corporately distinct from every other Cook Inlet sibling dispatched in this batch. Checked specifically against P7456 (Kenai-Anchorage Gas Pipeline, 70 mi) per the brief's explicit instruction: KKPL runs SOUTH from the Kenai area down the peninsula toward Kasilof/Anchor Point/Homer on Kachemak Bay (confirmed by DNR's route description -- parallels Kalifornsky Beach Road, the Sterling Highway, Cohoe Loop Road, and Oilwell Road, all on the southern Kenai Peninsula -- and by the routes-repo geojson, a single north-to-south trace from ~60.49N down to ~59.99N), whereas Kenai-Anchorage runs NORTH from the Kenai area toward Anchorage across Turnagain Arm -- opposite directions, serving different markets, not a duplicate or relabeling of the same asset. Also not a duplicate of P7450/P7458 (Beluga Pipeline, a separate historic line on the west/Beluga side of Cook Inlet and/or the post-2014 consolidated brand name for the whole four-pipeline system depending on which row), P7453 (Kenai Nikiski Pipeline/KNPL, a distinct certificate/CPCN 20-inch line), or P7455 (Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System/CIGGS, a gathering-class system) -- the 2014 RCA consolidation notice (Docket P-14-025) itself lists KBPL, Beluga Pipeline Company, KKPL, CIGGS, and KNPL as five SEPARATE pre-existing certificated entities being merged into one operating structure under KBPL/amended CPCN 668 (which, by elimination against the notice's list of CPCNs 'returned to the Commission' for CIGGS/KNPL/Beluga, appears to be KKPL's own pre-consolidation certificate) -- confirming these are five genuinely distinct historical pipeline systems now under common ownership/operation, not five records of the same pipe.

validity.recommendation: Have a human check whether EndLocation should read 'Happy Valley' rather than (or in addition to) 'Kasilof'. DNR's own text names TWO named extensions built onto this system -- 'the Happy Valley and Kasilof Extensions' -- and this researcher's own measurement of the routes-repo geojson (P7454.geojson: a single LineString, ~46 points, running from ~60.492N/-151.276W in the north down to ~59.987N/-151.488W in the south) places the mapped southern terminus within the Happy Valley CDP footprint (per Nominatim/OSM geocoding, used here only for orientation, not as a citable source) rather than within Kasilof's -- Kasilof proper lies noticeably further north of that terminus coordinate. This may mean the geojson traces the mainline + Happy Valley Extension and stops short of the separate, smaller-diameter (6.625-inch) Kasilof Extension DNR describes as its own ~4.2-mile branch, in which case 'Kasilof' as EndLocation is defensible as the system's southernmost named component even if the mapped route itself does not reach it. Left unresolved deliberately: this is a single-origin (DNR text) finding plus this researcher's own unpublished geometry measurement, which per this campaign's origin-counting rule never contributes a second origin, so no confident replacement value is proposed.
validity.researcher_notes: Alaska DNR DOG's Kenai Kachemak page states the system 'was built in three phases during 2003, 2004, and 2006, which include the Happy Valley and Kasilof Extensions,' and separately describes 'The 6.625-inch diameter Kasilof Extension is approximately 4.2 miles long, of which 4.1 miles are located on State lands' as one distinct component of the whole system -- implying a second, un-named-in-the-cell 'Happy Valley Extension' also exists as part of the same pipeline. The sheet's EndLocation='Kasilof' is a real, DNR-documented place-name for this system (kept in the fills[] record above as an honest reflection of the source), but it is not obviously the pipeline's true southernmost or otherwise most representative named terminus given DNR names Happy Valley too. Single origin (DNR); flagged as a spec/attribution concern for human review rather than silently changed.

cross_row_leads.facts: RCA Docket P-14-025 (2014 consolidation notice): 'Kenai Beluga Pipeline, LLC (KBPL), Beluga Pipeline Company (Beluga), Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, LLC (KKPL), Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System (CIGGS), and Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline (KNPL)' jointly applied to merge CPCN Nos. 448, 711, 668, and 689 into one certificate; 'the Applicants are all owned 100 percent, directly or indirectly, by Hilcorp Alaska, LLC'; KBPL proposed to operate the consolidated system under amended CPCN No. 668 (apparently KKPL's own pre-consolidation certificate, by elimination against the CPCNs of CIGGS/KNPL/Beluga being 'returned to the Commission'), with a single postage-stamp tariff of $0.2912/Mcf, effective on/around November 1, 2014 (Docket P-13-014 settlement/tariff). One of 'Beluga's' CPCN numbers (448, 711, or 689) belongs to Beluga Pipeline Company -- useful for pinning down this row's own pre-2014 certificate number.

Same RCA Docket P-14-025 consolidation facts as the P7450 lead above -- 'Beluga Pipeline Company' is one of the five entities merged into KBPL under amended CPCN 668. Additionally, the 2022 PHMSA Final Order (CPF No. 5-2021-023-NOPV, $73,900 penalty) discusses the 'Beluga Transmission Pipeline' by name -- bi-directional, tied to the BRU (Beluga River Unit) compressor, receiving 'West CIGGS sources,' with 'Kaloa Junction' as a described overpressure-protection location and PSV-10056/PSV X-028 valve compliance findings under Harvest Alaska, LLC's operatorship -- directly relevant if this row is the Beluga Transmission Pipeline specifically.

Same RCA Docket P-14-025 consolidation facts -- 'Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline (KNPL)' is named explicitly as one of the five pre-consolidation entities, 100% owned by Hilcorp Alaska LLC, its CPCN (one of 448/711/689) surrendered/returned to the Commission upon the 2014 consolidation under KBPL/amended CPCN 668.

Same RCA Docket P-14-025 consolidation facts -- 'Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System (CIGGS)' is named explicitly as one of the five pre-consolidation entities, 100% owned by Hilcorp Alaska LLC, its CPCN (one of 448/711/689) surrendered upon the 2014 consolidation. Separately, the 2022 PHMSA Final Order (CPF No. 5-2021-023-NOPV) discusses 'West CIGGS sources' feeding the Beluga Transmission Pipeline and PSV compliance findings involving the CIGGS system under Harvest Alaska, LLC's operatorship -- both documents are reserved here since they never name Kachemak/KKPL specifically (so were not used as P7454 refs) but concern this sibling row directly.

summary: P7454 (Kenai Beluga Pipeline / Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, KKPL) confirmed real, correctly classified (operating/Gas/transmission), and NOT a duplicate of sibling P7456 (Kenai-Anchorage, which runs north; KKPL runs south toward Kasilof/Homer) or of P7450/P7453/P7455/P7458 (five genuinely distinct pre-2014-consolidation certificated systems per RCA Docket P-14-025).
